byTheNumbers.title: The year in numbers
byTheNumbers.standfirst: Two in three Americans were online and seven in ten had a mobile phone, a long way from the flip phone's first years.

items.title: Population
items.summary: The United States had about 296 million people in 2005.

sources.label: World Bank, World Development Indicators: Population, total
Our World in Data: Population (UN World Population Prospects, HYDE)

items.title: Life expectancy at birth
items.summary: A baby born in 2005 could expect to live about 77.5 years.

items.title: Online
items.summary: About 68 percent of Americans used the internet in 2005.

items.title: Mobile phones

foodAndKitchen.scarcityNote: We could not find sourced 2005 food prices, appliance counts or meals.

clothingAndStyle.title: What people wore
clothingAndStyle.standfirst: Low-rise jeans and belly shirts ruled the mid-decade, and skinny jeans arrived.

items.title: Low-rise jeans
items.summary: Embroidered low-rise jeans were a popular women's trend from 2003 to 2006, worn with belly shirts and newsboy caps.

items.title: Skinny jeans
items.summary: Skinny jeans were introduced in 2005 and became popular in 2006.

items.title: Fast fashion
items.summary: In 2004 the fast-fashion retailer H&M collaborated with Karl Lagerfeld on a one-time collection that was a major success; fast fashion consumption was rising, with Zara among the new giants.

items.title: The 'It' items
items.summary: Velour tracksuits, Ugg boots, Von Dutch trucker hats and boldly logoed purses and sunglasses were sought-after in the mid-2000s, with fast-fashion copies widely available.

items.title: Hoodies and Crocs
items.summary: Hoodies were a staple of casual dress, and Crocs were a brief fad for all sexes in summer 2006.

gettingAround.title: Getting around
gettingAround.standfirst: In late August a million people left the Gulf Coast ahead of a hurricane.

items.title: Leaving New Orleans
items.summary: Before Hurricane Katrina made landfall on 29 August 2005, a mandatory evacuation of New Orleans was ordered on 28 August and a contraflow plan moved about one million people; about 80 percent of the city left, and Katrina displaced over a million people in all.

sensitivity.note: This item concerns a hurricane that killed more than a thousand people.

keepingInTouch.title: Keeping in touch
keepingInTouch.standfirst: A video site went online in February.
keepingInTouch.scarcityNote: We could not find sourced 2005 postage, text-message or call-rate figures; the sharing sites are in the spotlight.

leisureAndFun.title: Evenings, weekends and festivals
leisureAndFun.standfirst: New on television: a workplace comedy, an animated Last Airbender and a season of American Idol won by Carrie Underwood.

items.title: New shows
items.summary: American Dad! debuted on 6 February, Avatar: The Last Airbender on 21 February, The Office on 24 March and It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia on 4 August 2005.

items.title: American Idol
items.summary: Carrie Underwood won the fourth season of American Idol on 25 May 2005.

items.title: At the cinema
items.summary: Million Dollar Baby won Best Picture at the Academy Awards on 27 February; Star Wars: Episode III opened on 19 May and Madagascar on 27 May 2005.

items.title: Super Bowl XXXIX
items.summary: The New England Patriots beat the Philadelphia Eagles 24-21 in Super Bowl XXXIX on 6 February 2005.

items.title: A seventh Tour
items.summary: Lance Armstrong won a record seventh straight Tour de France on 24 July 2005.

spotlight.title: Sharing online and the camera phone
spotlight.standfirst: In 2005 a site for uploading and watching home video opened to the public, and by the end of the year it was serving 8 million views a day.

items.title: YouTube goes online
items.summary: YouTube was founded on 14 February 2005 by Chad Hurley, Jawed Karim and Steve Chen, former PayPal employees, and went online that month.

items.title: The first video
items.summary: The first video, 'Me at the zoo', showing Jawed Karim at the San Diego Zoo, was uploaded on 23 April 2005, when the public beta began; early clips were capped at 100 megabytes, about 30 seconds.

items.title: One million views
items.summary: By November 2005 a Nike advertisement featuring Ronaldinho was the first video to reach one million views.

items.title: Eight million a day
items.summary: When YouTube left beta in December 2005 it was getting 8 million views a day; by July 2006 it had 100 million views a day and 65,000 new videos uploaded daily.

items.title: Reddit
items.summary: Reddit launched on 23 June 2005.

spotlight.scarcityNote: We could not find sourced figures for camera-phone ownership or photo sharing in 2005, so the section is about video.
